sections.h2: Where is Limestone County, Alabama, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Limestone County is in the far north of Alabama on the Tennessee line, with Athens as the county seat and the largest city that lies entirely inside the county. The territorial legislature established it on February 6, 1818, and it takes its name from Limestone Creek.

It covers 607 square miles, of which 560 are land and 47 are water, making it the third smallest Alabama county by land area. The Tennessee River and the Elk River both run through it, and part of the Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the county. Neighbors include Giles and Lincoln counties in Tennessee, Madison County to the east, and Morgan, Lawrence and Lauderdale counties to the south and west.

The county is part of the Huntsville metropolitan area, so Huntsville-area prices and jobs influence what happens here.

sections.h2: How fast is Limestone County growing?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 103,570 people, a jump of about 25% from 2010, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 122,928.

The 2020 census also found 42,692 housing units, with 7.8% vacant and 76.5% of occupied homes owner-occupied. Roughly three in four occupied homes are lived in by their owners, so most sales involve a single-family home with an owner-occupant behind it.

sections.h2: Which cities, towns and schools make up Limestone County?
sections.html:
Athens, with 25,406 residents in 2020, is the largest city entirely inside the county. The city of Madison is second in population and Huntsville is third, though both are mostly in Madison County. Decatur also touches the county, although it lies mostly in Morgan County.

The incorporated towns are Ardmore, Elkmont, Lester and Mooresville, and Mooresville is the smallest with 47 people in 2020. Unincorporated communities include Belle Mina, Capshaw, Tanner, Veto and Greenbrier.

Five public school systems serve the county:

  • Limestone County Schools, for most areas outside the cities.
  • Athens City Schools.
  • Decatur City Schools.
  • Huntsville City Schools.
  • Madison City Schools.

Higher education in the area includes Athens State University and Calhoun Community College, whose campus is in the southern part of the county near Decatur.

sections.h2: How do roads and airports affect a Limestone County sale?
sections.html:
Limestone County is crossed by Interstate 65, Interstate 565, U.S. 31 and U.S. 72, along with state routes 20, 53, 99, 127 and 251. Freight rail runs on a CSX north-south line and a Norfolk Southern east-west line.

Huntsville International Airport is the closest major commercial airport, about 23 miles east of the county. Nashville is roughly 104 miles to the north.

Where a house sits relative to those highways is one of the facts a buyer will weigh, so mention the nearest interchange when you describe a property.

sections.h2: When are Limestone County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Property taxes in Limestone County follow the state calendar: due October 1 and delinquent after the end of the year. The Alabama Department of Revenue summarizes the full sequence, which runs from the October 1 due date through delinquency on January 1, a turnover to probate court in February, newspaper advertising in April and the tax sale in May.

The county's Revenue Commissioner runs a Citizen Access Portal at limestonerevenue.net, which the office describes as a place to look up real estate and business personal property information. Use it to see the parcel number, owner and bill before you call the office about a payoff.

A tax bill in Alabama combines state, county, municipal and school district levies, so a home inside Athens and a home in the unincorporated county are not billed the same way. Always check the exact parcel instead of comparing two neighbors by price alone.

sections.h2: What can reduce a Limestone County tax bill?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one, and it applies to a single-family owner-occupied home on up to 160 acres that is your primary residence on the first day of the tax year. You apply at the county office.

  • Homeowners under 65 can receive up to $4,000 of assessed value off the state tax and, in the standard case, $2,000 off the county tax.
  • Owners 65 and older with a low income can qualify for broader relief, and a permanently and totally disabled owner can qualify at any age.
  • Blind owners can qualify at any age for state-level relief.

The exemptions are tied to the person who lives in the house. Sellers should not assume a buyer inherits yours, and heirs who keep a house need to file their own claim.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Limestone County property assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the county Board of Equalization, the body Alabama law uses to hear value disputes. Ask the Revenue Commissioner's office for the filing window each year, because it follows the date the county announces new values.

If the board does not change the value, section 40-3-25 of the Code of Alabama sets the next step. The appeal to circuit court has to be taken within 30 days of the board's final decision, with notice to the board secretary and the circuit clerk and a bond for costs. A jury can be requested within 10 days, and the loser may appeal to the Alabama Supreme Court within 42 days of the circuit judgment.

Limestone County makes up the 39th Judicial Circuit, which has two circuit judges and two district judges. The court also requires that the earlier year's tax be paid on time, or covered by a bond, for the appeal to proceed.

sections.h2: What happens after a Limestone County tax sale?
sections.html:
The buyer at a tax sale does not take final title right away, because Alabama gives the owner a chance to redeem. Under section 40-10-120, the owner, heirs, personal representatives, a mortgagee or anyone with a legal or equitable interest can redeem within three years of the sale.

A recorded mortgage holder gets an additional year from the date of a written notice from the purchaser. A minor or an incapacitated person has up to one year after the disability is removed. The statute also lets someone redeem part of the land sold.

  • If you own a house that was sold at tax sale, the three-year window is your main deadline.
  • If you inherited the home, heirs are named in the statute as people who can redeem.
  • If you plan to sell, the buyer has to deal with the open tax sale at closing.

We buy Limestone County houses in all of these situations, and we can talk through the numbers before any commitment.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Limestone County usually deal with?
sections.html:
The most common situations are inherited houses, rural acreage with an older home, and rentals that an owner no longer wants to manage. About half of the county's residents live in rural areas, so a house here may come with acreage and a longer drive to town, and those details shape what a buyer will pay.

Parts of the county sit along the Elk and Tennessee rivers, and a lender may ask extra questions about a property in that kind of setting. A cash purchase avoids that step.

The Limestone Revenue portal, the probate office and the title company each hold a piece of the file. We gather those pieces so you do not have to chase each office.

faqs.q: Where is the Limestone County, AL courthouse?
faqs.a: The county seat is Athens. Property tax matters go through the Limestone County Revenue Commissioner, which also runs a public portal at limestonerevenue.net.

faqs.q: When are Limestone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1 under the Alabama calendar, and they turn delinquent after the end of the year.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a Limestone County house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Three years from the date of sale in most cases, under section 40-10-120 of the Code of Alabama. Some lienholders and people with a legal disability get additional time.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal to circuit court?
faqs.a: 30 days after the Board of Equalization's final decision, under section 40-3-25. The taxes must also be paid or bonded to keep the appeal alive.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Limestone County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid balance is paid from the closing proceeds, so ask the Revenue Commissioner for a current payoff before you agree to a price.
